verifiedClaims: 3.1.1 root cause: LmdbBoundSimplifierOptimizer.java:53-59 captures only root BindingSet names; meet(Filter) :62-80 builds assured/possible from filter.getArg() (:66,:68) plus that set; simplifyBound :108-110 folds to FALSE when the name is not possible and :75-76 replaces the Filter with EmptySet. The visitor is an AbstractQueryModelVisitor whose meet(Exists) (:223-224) and meet(Lateral) (:328) descend into the EXISTS body / LATERAL right arg.

Parent-chain analysis is viable: meet(Filter) calls super.meet(filter) first (:63) so inner filters are processed while the tree is intact; parent pointers are maintained by Filter.setCondition (Filter.java:54), SubQueryValueOperator.setSubQuery (:42) and UnaryValueOperator.setArg (:54); LmdbQueryOptimizerPipeline.withParentChecks inserts ParentReferenceChecker between optimizers when asserts are enabled, so a broken chain fails tests. Projection.isSubquery() exists (Projection.java:139).

3.1.2 root cause: LmdbFilterSimplifierOptimizer.java:525-527 accepts on rightArg.getBindingNames() (possible) and :545-547 builds Join(L, Join(anchor, R)); the method is static with no outer/incoming names. The filter is retained afterwards via shouldRetainMandatoryOptionalFilter (:633-637) unless the alias case, so the spurious row is produced exactly as described. Single call chain: FilterMerger.meet(Filter) :201 -> rewriteSmallLiteralFilterAnchors :336 -> makeUnboundRejectingOptionalsMandatory :348/:498 -> :507. The new guard at :525 sits before both the hoist (:540) and plain (:545) branches, so it covers all paths.

c3_mandatoryOptionalAnchorInsideExistsWithCorrelatedWitness reaches makeOptionalBindingMandatory because LmdbNullRejectingOptionalSupport.isBarrierFreeNode :254-255 rejects the scope-changed right arg -> rewrite() returns null at :72-74, and the right arg is a StatementPattern that ASSURES ?w, so the assured-only check alone would not block it; the outerVisible guard is genuinely required for this case.

3.1.3 root cause: LmdbFilterSimplifierOptimizer.optimize :134-136 derives incomingBindingNames from the root only, optimizeScope :148-163 passes the same set into every VariableScopeChange subtree, FilterMerger.meet(Filter) :191-192 is the ONLY production caller of LmdbNullRejectingOptionalSupport.rewrite (rg over core/*/main), and selectUnboundWitness :215-222 is the sole correlation guard. Design's one-call-site change is therefore complete for this rule.

3.1.4 root cause: isSmallLiteralAnchorCandidate :483 accepts SameTerm; LmdbJoinPlanSupport.smallLiteralFilterAnchor :199-201 and collectOrEqualityAnchorValues :356-358 collect SameTerm constants; canMaterializeObjectFilterAnchor :1345-1365 never inspects the operator; expandFiniteAnchor :1200-1233 value-expands integers (:1213-1216), booleans (:1217-1218) and normalises dateTime to the Z form (:1221-1226); rewriteSmallLiteralFilterAnchors :414-416 drops the condition when remainingConditions is empty. The OPTIONAL variants take the :1178-1181 shortcut only for safe values, so numeric/boolean sameTerm falls through to the guarantee path as described. exactStoredTermFilterAnchor already retains the condition (:382), so it is already sound for sameTerm.

3.1.5 root cause: RdfTermDomain.Fact :36-47 has no boolean canonicity fact; UNIVERSAL_FACT_MASK :63-64 is ANDed in joinObserved :219 so a new universal fact behaves as designed; canMaterializeObjectFilterAnchor's boolean branch :1357-1360 only checks hasDatatype(BOOLEAN); addBooleanAnchorValues :1280-1291 emits {true,1}/{false,0}. XSD_FACT_OFFSET = Fact.values().length (:55) so appending a Fact shifts every datatype bit and the persisted mask needs the PREDICATE_OBJECT_DOMAINS_VERSION bump (TripleStore.java:157, currently rdf-term-domain-v4); the FACT_COUNT <= 62 guard (:56,:62) has headroom (11+47 -> 12+47). toString iterates Fact ordinals then datatypes (RdfTermDomain.toString), so the only affected test string is LmdbPredicateObjectDomainIndexTest:520-521 (the sole 'BOOLEAN]' assertion in core/sail/lmdb/src/test).

3.1.6 root cause: ValueStore.valueIDCache is ConcurrentCache<LmdbValue,Long> (:197); getId consults it at :1996 before value2data/findId (:2038-2041); findId is byte-exact (mdb_get on the encoding :1387-1391, hash path bufferEquals :1428-1430); BatchIdStorer.findSmallId :1668-1670 is byte-exact and creates a new id on miss (storeValues :2075-2140 -> findIds); literal2data :2830-2833 encodes the tag bytes verbatim; clearCaches :2634-2645 empties valueIDCache; AbstractLiteral.equals compares language with equalsIgnoreCase (:200-206) with hashCode = label hash (:182-184), and LmdbLiteral.equals falls back to super.equals when ids are unknown/other revision (LmdbLiteral.java:277-292). Values.packLiteral never inlines rdf:langString (asXSDDatatypeOrNull null -> 0L, Values.java:70-74). literal2legacy (:2804-2810) also goes through literal2data, so one canonicalisation point in literal2data covers both encodings.

3.5 root cause: TripleStore.commitDurableStatementBatch :3288-3296 orders flushPendingRdfTermDomains -> mdb_txn_commit -> applyPendingRdfTermDomainCacheUpdates; the second apply (:3410), txnManager.reset (:3413) and dataRevision++ (:3415) also run after the commit. Cache staging only happens via writeRdfTermDomain (:807), deleteRdfTermDomain (:832) and stageRdfTermDomainCacheClear (:846, rebuild only). TxnManager.createReadTxn (:145 -> :171) does NOT take lockManager.readLock (only doWith does, :224-236) and LmdbSailDataset opens its txn directly (LmdbSailStore.java:3291; datasets created at :1490/:1985 without the lock), so the window is real. combine() == joinObserved (RdfTermDomain) so runtime updates only weaken; rebuildRdfTermDomains/rebuildMarkedRdfTermDomains are only called from initializeRdfTermDomains (:413,:423 -> :553) before readers exist. The planner reads the volatile cache via LmdbEstimatorStorageAccess.rdfTermDomain :258-268 -> TripleStore.getRdfTermDomain :705-718.

Pipeline order confirmed (LmdbQueryOptimizerPipeline.java:243-265): FilterOptimizer(null,false,false) -> LmdbBoundSimplifierOptimizer -> LmdbSetSemantics -> LmdbFilterSimplifierOptimizer(stats, committedEvidenceUsable) -> LmdbFilterHoist; the same list is used by both requestBoundOptimizers() and getOptimizers(). LmdbPipelinePlanCache.BindingIdentity (:511-520, used at pipeline :166) keys on incoming binding names AND values, so root-frame incoming-name dependence is cache-safe.

Existing tests: LmdbBoundSimplifierOptimizerTest (4 tests, :45-75) use names local to the filter arg; preSketchSimplifiesBoundInsideOptionalRightSide (:68) has optName assured by the right arg itself -> still folds to TRUE. LmdbFilterSimplifierOptimizerTest mandatory-optional tests (:866-1000) use StatementPattern right args (assured) or an Extension right arg that is already rejected at :530-532 before the new guard -> unaffected. lang-3 in the W3C data-r2 suite (q-lang-3.rq `?x :p "string"@EN` over data-builtin-2.ttl `"string"@en`) is exactly the plain-pattern case and today passes only because the cache is warm right after loading; it must keep passing under either 3.1.6 option.

issues.issue: The prescribed AnchorEquality classification is unsound for mixed disjunctions: 'mixed Or of SameTerm and Compare.EQ counts as TERM, i.e. the strictest' combined with the preferred option 'materialize the exact-term anchor and RETAIN the condition'. For `?s :v ?o FILTER(sameTerm(?o, 7) || ?o = 8)` over {:s1 :v "7"^^xsd:int, :s2 :v "8"^^xsd:int} the correct answer is [s2] (value-equal to 8). collectOrEqualityAnchorValues (LmdbJoinPlanSupport.java:356-358) collects both constants into one anchor {7^^integer, 8^^integer}; a term-exact (unexpanded) anchor excludes :s2's "8"^^xsd:int, and the retained filter cannot bring the row back. Expanding LESS than the value-equal family is only sound when every disjunct is sameTerm; the design's own additional test ('sameTerm(?o, 7) || ?o = 8 ... only the row value-equal to 8') would go red under the prescribed rule.
issues.suggestion: Invert the rule: the presence of SameTerm anywhere in the condition means the FILTER must be RETAINED (never dropped); the anchor may then be the value-expanded superset as today (superset + retained filter is always sound) or omitted. Only for a pure all-SameTerm condition may the anchor be unexpanded. Concretely: in rewriteSmallLiteralFilterAnchors treat containsSameTerm(condition) like the exactStoredTermFilterAnchor pattern (anchors.add(...); remainingConditions.add(condition)) and skip the :385-387 drop only when the anchor is not term-exact-equivalent. Keep the mixed-Or test and add `sameTerm(?o,7) || ?o = 8` with stored "8"^^xsd:int and "8"^^xsd:integer -> both rows.

issues.issue: Rule (d) (sub-SELECT barrier: frames further out still contribute to POSSIBLE) regresses a spec-correct answer to the executor's 3.4.3 leak. Query `SELECT ?s ?o { ?s :p ?x { SELECT ?o WHERE { ?s :q ?o FILTER(BOUND(?x)) } } }` over {:s1 :p :v1, :s1 :q :o1}: per SPARQL the sub-select is evaluated independently, BOUND(?x) is false, result []. Today LmdbBoundSimplifierOptimizer folds it to FALSE (:108-110) because ?x is not possible in the inner arg, giving the spec answer; after the design, ?x becomes 'possible' from the outer Join frame, the fold is suppressed, and ProjectionQueryEvaluationStep passes the parent row into the sub-select (raw notes 3.4.3), so BOUND(?x) is TRUE at runtime and a wrong row is returned. The same applies inside EXISTS bodies that contain a sub-select. The 'possible names only block' principle is right for the FilterSimplifier consumers (blocking is the safe direction) but wrong for BOUND->FALSE folding, where the spec-correct fold is what is being blocked.
issues.suggestion: Make OuterScopeBindings report the sub-select barrier explicitly (e.g. a third field `barrierPossible` or a mode flag). LmdbBoundSimplifierOptimizer should treat an isSubquery() Projection as a hard barrier (stop the walk: neither possible nor assured from outside), which keeps today's spec-correct fold; LmdbFilterSimplifierOptimizer consumers keep the conservative possible-only propagation. Add the query above as a control that must stay [] in both LMDB pipelines, and document that once wp5 fixes 3.4.3 the two behaviours coincide.

issues.issue: The legacy-store plan ('on a canonical miss retry findId with the exact legacy bytes') cannot repair stores that ALREADY contain two ids for case variants, which is exactly what the confirmed create-path bug produces (ValueStore.storeValues :2075-2140 -> BatchIdStorer.findSmallId :1668-1670 creates a second id when the cache is cold). Scenario: a pre-fix store holds :a :label "abc"@en (id1, written cold) and :b :label "abc"@EN (id2, written after a restart). After the fix, getId("abc"@EN) canonicalises to id1 and `?s :label "abc"@EN` returns only :a, while before the fix (warm) it could return either subset depending on which variant was cached first. Neither fallback-on-miss nor 're-key the LITERAL_VALUE entry' merges id2's triple-index entries into id1; a real migration must rewrite every triple referencing id2 (all indexes plus the value refcount/hash sidecar), which is far larger than the design's 'scan LITERAL_VALUE entries and re-key' suggests. The design also leaves Option A vs B open although Option A changes observable data (lang(?x) / Rio export from an LMDB store return "en-us" for stored "en-US"); W3C compliance is safe (lang-case-insensitive-eq/ne and open-eq-07..12 compare via case-insensitive Literal.equals; no test compares lang() output against an uppercase simple literal), but downstream users comparing str(lang(?x)) case-sensitively would see a behaviour change.
issues.suggestion: Prefer Option B (canonical lowercased key, original bytes as id->data payload; hash path compares canonicalLanguageKey(payload) with canonicalLanguageKey(query)). For legacy stores, persist a StoreProperties flag and on first open of a pre-fix store run a real merge migration in the same lifecycle slot as rebuildRdfTermDomains: enumerate LITERAL_VALUE entries whose canonical key collides, pick a survivor id, rewrite triples of the losers across all indexes and delete the loser value entries; if that is too costly, refuse to enable the canonical lookup (keep byte-exact + cache) and log a warning rather than silently returning a subset. Add a ValueStoreTest that builds the duplicate-id fixture with the fix disabled and asserts a full result after migration.

issues.issue: The proposed split (publish weakenings before commit, keep post-commit publication for the clear/rebuild case) guards a path that cannot occur at commit time: stageRdfTermDomainCacheClear is only reached from rebuildRdfTermDomains (:491) and rebuild is only invoked from initializeRdfTermDomains (:413,:423) before any reader exists; rebuildMarkedRdfTermDomains stages ordinary WRITES (via writeRdfTermDomain :807), not a clear, so the clear flag would not even distinguish it. The split adds complexity without covering anything. Also note the reorder leaves pendingRdfTermDomainCacheWrites populated until the finally block (:3440), so the second call at :3410 re-applies the same entries (idempotent, as the design says) and a failed commit leaves the heap cache weaker than disk until reopen (sound).
issues.suggestion: Simply move applyPendingRdfTermDomainCacheUpdates() before E(mdb_txn_commit(txn)) unconditionally and add an assertion/javadoc that any future strengthening path (rebuild at runtime) must publish after commit; keep the :3410 call. Add the deterministic test hook the design lists and a test that a failed commit does not throw from the cache path.

issues.issue: Rule (c) adds left possible names for the right arg of Union and Difference. Union right args are never correlated and MINUS right args are not evaluated with left bindings per spec; adding them is harmless (blocking only) but needlessly suppresses spec-correct BOUND->FALSE folds such as `?s :p ?x MINUS { ?s :q ?o FILTER(BOUND(?x)) }` (spec: all rows). Rule (b) uses left.getBindingNames() for LATERAL although Lateral.getRightInputBindingNames() (Lateral.java:50-52) is the model's own declaration of what flows into the right arg.
issues.suggestion: Restrict rule (c) to Join and LeftJoin right args; use Lateral.getRightInputBindingNames() for possible and intersect it with left.getAssuredBindingNames() for assured.

issues.issue: The control repro c1_boundInsideNestedOptionalGroupIsFalseBySpec stays green after the fix only because FilterIterator.filterScopeBindingNames (FilterIterator.java:725-752) hides outer bindings for a scope-changed Filter (the walk breaks at :741 on the first iteration). This relies on (a) the inner Filter keeping its variable-scope-change flag through FilterOptimizer/FilterMerger (FilterMerger.canMerge/setArg at :187-190 could merge a scope-changed child into a non-scope-changed parent) and (b) the packed physical plan evaluating that node through FilterIterator rather than a fused operator. The design asserts the executor 'yields the spec answer as the oracle shows' but the oracle is the standard pipeline, not the LMDB physical plan.
issues.suggestion: Keep the control test and add an algebra-level assertion in LmdbBoundSimplifierOptimizerTest that a scope-changed Filter on a LeftJoin right side is left untouched (not folded either way); verify canMerge refuses to merge across differing scope flags; run the control under both executors as the design already plans.

issues.issue: The top-level disjunction repro methods (c5_sameTermDisjunctionIsNotValueEquality, c5_sameTermBooleanDisjunctionIsNotValueEquality) are not proven to exercise the code this WP changes: in the LMDB pipeline DISJUNCTIVE_CONSTRAINT_OPTIMIZER and SAME_TERM_FILTER_OPTIMIZER run before LmdbFilterSimplifierOptimizer (LmdbQueryOptimizerPipeline.java:253-255) and should have split/inlined the sameTerm constants; the design itself lists 'why did it reach the anchor path' as an open question. If the row comes from a packed rule (wp2 3.2.4) these two tests will stay red after this WP's fix and cannot serve as its Hit Proof. The OPTIONAL variants (c5_sameTermIntegerViaNullRejectedOptional / Boolean) do exercise :1178-1181 -> :1183 -> expandFiniteAnchor and are valid Hit Proof.
issues.suggestion: Before implementing, capture the Explanation.Level.Optimized plan of the two disjunction repros; if the anchor is produced by PackedLogicalRuleProgram, move those two methods to wp2's list and keep only the OPTIONAL variants plus the new algebra-level LmdbFilterSimplifierOptimizerTest cases as this WP's evidence.

issues.issue: Adding CANONICAL_BOOLEAN to UNIVERSAL_FACT_MASK also feeds degradationCandidateMask (TripleStore.updateRdfTermDomain :760-780): every boolean predicate that later observes a non-canonical form will be marked for rebuild, and the version bump forces a full rebuildRdfTermDomains on first open of every existing store (initializeRdfTermDomains :421-425). The design mentions the rebuild but not that with predicateGuaranteeIndexAutoRebuild=false and properties.isLoaded() (:418-421) the guarantees are CLEARED instead, so upgraded stores with auto-rebuild disabled silently lose all guarantee-based anchors until an operator intervenes.
issues.suggestion: Call out the upgrade behaviour for both auto-rebuild settings in the change note; add the 'downgradeGuaranteeMetadata' upgrade test for both settings (LmdbPredicateObjectDomainIndexTest helper at :708) and assert the explain string / row count in each.

missedFindings: None of the in-scope review findings (3.1.1-3.1.6, 3.5 race) is skipped. One under-treatment: the review's 3.1.6 text says the plain-pattern form fails cold in the standard pipeline; the W3C data-r2 test 'lang-3' (testcases-sparql-1.0-w3c/data-r2/expr-builtin/q-lang-3.rq over data-builtin-2.ttl, run against LMDB via SPARQL10QueryComplianceTest) is an existing compliance test for exactly this and currently passes only because the cache is warm immediately after load; the design should list it as the regression guard for 3.1.6 and add a cold-reopen variant.

3.1.6 design omits that a pre-fix store can already hold TWO ids for one term (create path :2113-2140 cold), so the pre-existing LmdbLiteral.equals id-comparison (LmdbLiteral.java:283-289) makes DISTINCT/GROUP BY/joins treat "abc"@en and "abc"@EN as different in both pipelines; fixing lookups without merging ids leaves that inconsistency in legacy stores.
semanticRegressionRisks: 3.1.4 as prescribed: `SELECT ?s { ?s :v ?o FILTER(sameTerm(?o, 7) || ?o = 8) }` over {:s1 :v "7"^^xsd:int, :s2 :v "8"^^xsd:int} -> expected [s2]; TERM classification with a term-exact anchor {7^^integer, 8^^integer} returns [] (row lost). Any mixed sameTerm/= or sameTerm/IN disjunction is affected.

3.1.1 rule (d): `SELECT ?s ?o { ?s :p ?x { SELECT ?o WHERE { ?s :q ?o FILTER(BOUND(?x)) } } }` over {:s1 :p :v1, :s1 :q :o1} -> spec []; today LMDB returns [] via the fold; after the design the fold is suppressed and the 3.4.3 executor leak yields a row. Same for `FILTER EXISTS { SELECT ?o { ... FILTER(BOUND(?x)) } }` shapes.
3.1.1 rule (c) over-blocking (not wrong, but lost sound fold): `?s :p ?x MINUS { ?s :q ?o FILTER(BOUND(?x)) }` and Union right args lose the BOUND->FALSE fold and fall back to the executor.

3.1.6 Option A: `SELECT (lang(?o) AS ?l) { ?s :label ?o }` over stored "x"@en-US returns "en-us" instead of "en-US" (RDF 1.1-permitted but user-visible; Rio export from LMDB changes). Option A legacy fallback: stores already holding two ids for case variants return a strict subset of matching triples for the canonical lookup.
3.1.2 guard is sound for the listed shapes; a lost optimisation is only the sub-select / nested-group / Union-with-one-branch right args, which were unsound anyway.

3.5 reorder: a failed mdb_txn_commit now leaves the heap cache weaker than disk until reopen (sound, may surprise heap-vs-disk equality tests such as LmdbPredicateObjectDomainIndexTest#predicateGuaranteesStayHeapResidentAndSynchronizedWithDisk if extended to failure paths).
